tools.name: AIS Hub
tools.desc: Raw AIS data feed for technical users requiring direct access to transmission data.

tools.name: Black Sea MoU
tools.desc: Black Sea region port state control inspection records.
tools.opsec: PSC databases are public; no registration required for most MoU portals.
tools.reliability: PSC records cover safety compliance only; they do not address cargo legality or sanctions status.

tools.name: Companies House
tools.desc: UK entity filings including the Persons with Significant Control register. Used to identify ultimate beneficial owners of UK-registered companies.
tools.reliability: Nominee directors are placeholders, not beneficial owners; verify control structure before attribution.

tools.name: Copernicus Open Access Hub
tools.desc: European Space Agency hub for Sentinel-1 SAR imagery. Used to obtain radar returns covering vessel positions during AIS gap periods.
tools.opsec: Treat SAR imagery coordinates as sensitive; handle with the same care as source material.
tools.reliability: SAR returns can be ambiguous; hull size matching requires expert interpretation.

tools.name: EMSA EMCIP
tools.desc: European maritime casualty database. Returns European casualty investigation summaries by vessel name and incident year.

tools.name: Equasis
tools.desc: IMO-endorsed registry providing verified information on commercial vessels including registered owner, ship manager, flag state, class society, and port state control inspection history.
tools.opsec: Equasis requires free registration; use an investigation-dedicated email account. Equasis logs search activity; treat each query as potentially visible. Search from a dedicated research browser profile.
tools.reliability: Ownership data reflects registration records, not verified beneficial ownership. Inspection records show detentions, not convictions; do not conflate the two. Aggregates PSC inspection data across all major MoUs but may lag individual portal updates by days; cross-reference against the originating MoU portal for accuracy. Cross-reference all ownership data against at least two independent registries. Never rely on vessel name alone; always anchor queries to the IMO number.

tools.name: EU Consolidated Sanctions List
tools.desc: Consolidated list of persons, groups, and entities subject to EU financial sanctions.

tools.name: Fleetmon
tools.desc: AIS replay and incident event log. Surfaces crowd-sourced and AIS-derived incident records and prior detentions for a given vessel.
tools.opsec: Download AIS replay data before it ages off free-tier archives.

tools.name: Global Fishing Watch
tools.desc: AIS gap analysis and dark vessel detection. Maintains AIS reception independent of commercial platforms, enabling cross-validation of gap periods.
tools.reliability: A gap visible on Global Fishing Watch but not on a commercial AIS platform indicates selective transmission rather than technical failure. Treat dark vessel behaviour as requiring explanation; it does not confirm illicit activity.

tools.name: ICIJ Offshore Leaks
tools.desc: Searchable database covering Panama Papers, Pandora Papers, and related leak datasets. Used for tracing beneficial ownership through offshore structures.

tools.name: IMO GISIS
tools.desc: IMO Global Integrated Shipping Information System. Houses the marine casualties module containing formal flag-state casualty filings and detention records.
tools.opsec: Save IMO casualty report PDFs immediately; documents are sometimes removed.
tools.reliability: Flag-state reports are sometimes filed late; delay does not always indicate concealment.

tools.name: ITU MARS
tools.desc: Official MMSI-to-flag-state registration database. Used to verify that an MMSI prefix matches the declared flag state.
tools.reliability: An MMSI prefix that does not match the declared flag state is an indicator of identity manipulation.

tools.name: Kpler
tools.desc: Commodity flow tracking and vessel cargo history. Returns declared cargo type and volume by voyage.

tools.name: Lloyd's List Intelligence
tools.desc: Vessel ownership history and corporate links. Used to identify previous owners and flag-state changes that may signal restructuring.
tools.opsec: Never query paid databases using a target-linked email.

tools.name: MAIB Casualty Reports
tools.desc: UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch formal investigation reports.
tools.opsec: Do not contact flag-state authorities from a byline-linked email address.

tools.name: MarineTraffic
tools.cost: Free tier; paid tiers for historical playback and additional features.
tools.desc: Real-time AIS feed and historical playback. The default first stop for vessel position and voyage history.
tools.opsec: MarineTraffic logs IP addresses. Route queries through a VPN. Avoid querying the same MMSI repeatedly from the same IP; rate-limit manually. Use a dedicated browser profile for maritime investigations.
tools.reliability: AIS position reflects transponder data, not verified GPS, and can be manually entered incorrectly. AIS relay stations can introduce a position lag of up to 30 minutes. Reception gaps are common in remote ocean areas; coverage is not global.

tools.name: NTSB Marine Casualty Reports
tools.desc: US National Transportation Safety Board marine casualty investigation reports.
tools.opsec: Do not contact flag-state authorities from a byline-linked email address.

tools.name: OFAC SDN List
tools.desc: US Treasury Specially Designated Nationals list. Returns US-designated vessels with IMO numbers and supports filtering by sanctions program.
tools.opsec: Segregate sanctions database queries from your primary research profile. Download OFAC SDN updates locally; the list changes without notice.
tools.reliability: Historical sanctions listings may predate vessel name recycling; confirm current designation status. Vessels with sanctioned-entity names that are distinct registered ships exist; verify by IMO.

tools.name: OpenCorporates
tools.cost: Free web search; paid tiers for API access.
tools.desc: Largest open database of company registrations across 140+ jurisdictions. Used for tracing corporate layers and identifying directors and shareholders.
tools.reliability: Identically named companies in different jurisdictions exist; confirm registration numbers. Historical ownership records change frequently after incidents.

tools.name: OpenSanctions
tools.cost: Free web access; paid tiers for bulk and API.
tools.desc: Cross-reference platform for screening individuals and entities against consolidated sanctions lists from multiple jurisdictions.

tools.name: Paris MoU
tools.desc: European and North Atlantic port state control inspection database. Publishes annual flag state performance rankings used to assess detention risk.
tools.opsec: PSC databases are public; no registration required for most MoU portals.
tools.reliability: High deficiency counts in some MoU regions reflect stricter inspection regimes, not worse vessels. Flag state ranking data reflects aggregate fleet performance, not individual vessel quality. PSC records cover safety compliance only; they do not address cargo legality or sanctions status.

tools.name: SkyTruth
tools.desc: Satellite-based vessel detection and dark ship alerts. Used to surface vessels operating without AIS transmission.

tools.name: TankerTrackers
tools.desc: Specialist STS event tracking and satellite integration. Returns logged STS events with date, location, and partner vessel.
tools.opsec: Never request satellite tasking from a byline-linked account.

tools.name: Tokyo MoU
tools.desc: Asia-Pacific port state control inspection database. Publishes annual flag state performance rankings used to assess detention risk.
tools.opsec: PSC databases are public; no registration required for most MoU portals.
tools.reliability: High deficiency counts in some MoU regions reflect stricter inspection regimes, not worse vessels. Flag state ranking data reflects aggregate fleet performance, not individual vessel quality. PSC records cover safety compliance only; they do not address cargo legality or sanctions status.

tools.name: UK OFSI Sanctions List
tools.desc: UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation consolidated list. Used alongside OFAC and EU lists for full sanctions screening coverage.

tools.name: UN Comtrade
tools.desc: Trade flow data used to cross-check declared cargo volumes against reporter-country and commodity-code declarations.

tools.name: UN Consolidated Sanctions List
tools.desc: United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list. Confirms designation status across all UN sanctions regimes.

tools.name: US Coast Guard PSIX
tools.desc: US Coast Guard Port State Information Exchange. Independent inspection records for vessels operating in US waters, not always captured by other MoUs.
tools.opsec: PSC databases are public; no registration required for most MoU portals.
tools.reliability: PSC records cover safety compliance only; they do not address cargo legality or sanctions status.

tools.name: VesselFinder
tools.desc: Alternative AIS source used to cross-reference position data and flag discrepancies in primary feeds.

tools.name: VIIRS Boat Detection (NASA FIRMS)
tools.desc: Nighttime lights data from NASA. Provides a third independent position signal for nocturnal AIS gaps in known fishing or transfer zones.

tools.name: Wayback Machine
tools.desc: Internet Archive snapshot service. Used to preserve sanctions designation pages, official report pages, and key company pages against later removal.

tools.name: Weather Underground History
tools.desc: Historical hourly meteorological records by station and date. Used to reconstruct wind, visibility, and sea-state conditions at incident time.
tools.reliability: Verify proximity of the weather station to the incident coordinates before treating records as evidence.

tools.name: Windward
tools.desc: Commercial AIS risk platform with AI-flagged STS events and behavioural risk scoring.

tools.name: World-Check (Refinitiv)
tools.desc: PEP and sanctions screening database for individuals and entities.
tools.opsec: Never query paid databases using a target-linked email.

tools.name: SonicVisualiser
tools.desc: Layer-based audio annotation and spectrogram analysis tool favoured in forensic workflows for producing annotated exports.

tools.name: Merlin Bird ID
tools.desc: Cornell Lab audio identification app that maps identified bird species against their geographic range, used for acoustic geolocation in recordings.
tools.reliability: Species range data reduces but does not eliminate locational ambiguity; cosmopolitan species appear across wide ranges.

tools.name: xeno-canto
tools.desc: Global repository of bird and wildlife sound recordings used for comparative species identification in acoustic geolocation workflows.
tools.opsec: Fauna recordings from online platforms may carry metadata from a location different from the audio's geographic origin.

tools.name: Hive Moderation AI Detector
tools.cost: Paid; per-file pricing via dashboard or API.
tools.desc: Multi-modal AI-generated content detector covering images, video, and audio with per-file confidence scores across generation classes.
tools.opsec: Confirm the platform's data retention policy before uploading evidential media. Record the exact API build version used at time of analysis.
tools.reliability: Treat any single detector result as a corroborating signal, not a conclusion; layer with at least one additional detector.

tools.name: Optic
tools.cost: Paid; web interface and API access.
tools.desc: AI-generated image and video detector cited in Reuters Institute and GIJN comparative testing; returns detection scores with visual overlay highlighting flagged regions.
tools.opsec: Confirm the platform's data retention policy before uploading evidential media.
tools.reliability: Cited in published comparative evaluations (Reuters Institute; GIJN). Detectors trained on specific generation models may not recognise output from newer architectures.

tools.name: Illuminarty
tools.desc: Image-focused AI probability scorer used as a cross-check source alongside higher-confidence commercial detectors.
tools.reliability: Use as a secondary cross-check; heavy JPEG compression or low-resolution crops reduce accuracy across all detectors.

tools.name: InVID / WeVerify
tools.desc: Browser extension providing metadata inspection, reverse image search, and keyframe extraction for video verification workflows.

tools.name: C2PA Content Credentials Inspector
tools.desc: Reads embedded C2PA provenance metadata in media files where watermarking has been applied at capture; documents whether credentials are present, absent, or stripped.
tools.opsec: C2PA credentials are frequently stripped by social media platforms on upload; their absence is not evidence of fabrication.
tools.reliability: Absence of credentials does not indicate AI generation. Presence confirms only that provenance was recorded at capture, not that content is authentic.

tools.name: FAA Aircraft Registry
tools.desc: Authoritative US N-number registration search with ownership history and airworthiness records maintained by the Federal Aviation Administration.
tools.opsec: Route all registry searches through a VPN to avoid alerting subjects. Document the registration date, jurisdiction, and source URL for every record retrieved.
tools.reliability: Trust and LLC registrations are standard US aviation practice and do not indicate concealment without additional indicators. Historical registry data may lag real ownership changes by weeks.

tools.name: ADS-B Exchange
tools.desc: Unfiltered global flight tracking platform that does not honour operator removal requests, making it the primary source for investigators tracking sensitive aircraft.
tools.opsec: Use as the primary tracking source precisely because operators cannot suppress data.
tools.reliability: ADS-B gaps over ocean or in airspace with limited receiver coverage do not indicate intentional flight suppression. (ADS-B Exchange platform documentation, adsbexchange.com/what-is-the-exchange)

tools.name: FlightAware
tools.cost: Free tier available; operators can pay for suppression.
tools.desc: Global flight tracking platform with ownership lookup; operators can pay to suppress visibility, so cross-reference against ADS-B Exchange for sensitive investigations.
tools.opsec: Do not rely on FlightAware alone; operators can pay to remove their aircraft from results.
tools.reliability: Operator suppression is a documented feature; absence of a record does not confirm a flight did not occur.

tools.name: Icarus Flights
tools.desc: Transponder data, ownership records, and area-based search designed specifically for investigative use; introduced by C4ADS at GIJC21.

tools.name: Rzjets / PlaneLogger
tools.desc: Community-maintained databases of business jet registrations and ownership records across jurisdictions, used for multi-jurisdiction registration history searches.
tools.reliability: Identical company names in different jurisdictions can produce erroneous ownership linkages without MSN verification.

tools.name: OCCRP Aleph
tools.desc: Cross-source search platform covering 340 million public entities across 141 countries, including persons-of-interest datasets, sanctions lists, and gazette records.
tools.opsec: Search from a research account with no personal identifiers. Route queries through a VPN.
tools.reliability: Database hits are starting points, not conclusions; the named party may be a nominee. Treat any match as requiring source-document verification.

tools.name: GLEIF Global LEI Index
tools.desc: Open corporate ownership database answering who-owns-whom via Level 2 LEI relationship records connecting direct and ultimate parent entities across jurisdictions.
tools.reliability: LEI coverage is strongest in regulated financial sectors; privately held or small entities may lack LEI records.

tools.name: LittleSis
tools.desc: US-focused relationship database mapping interlocks between corporate boards, political donors, and government officials.

tools.name: IPinfo.io
tools.cost: Free tier; paid tiers for higher API volume.
tools.desc: IP geolocation, ASN, organisation, VPN and proxy flag lookup with API access; the standard first stop for IP attribution.
tools.opsec: Never query a target IP directly from an operational device; route all lookups through a VPN. Treat city-level geolocation as approximate; country and ASN attribution are significantly more reliable.
tools.reliability: Cloud provider IP ownership (AWS, Google Cloud, Cloudflare) identifies the data centre operator, not the customer. Dynamic IPs are reassigned frequently; document the retrieval timestamp for every lookup.

tools.name: Shodan
tools.cost: Paid; free account provides limited results.
tools.desc: Internet-wide service-banner search engine indexing open ports, certificates, and device banners from IP addresses; essential for infrastructure fingerprinting.
tools.opsec: Shodan logs all queries; searching for a target IP reveals your interest to the platform. Route lookups through a VPN. Note the scan date on all results, as banners reflect the date of last Shodan scan, not the current state.
tools.reliability: Shared hosting environments place hundreds of unrelated websites on a single IP; co-hosting alone is insufficient for attribution.

tools.name: Censys
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid tiers for API access.
tools.desc: Certificate transparency and service data indexed by IP; complementary to Shodan for mapping shared SSL certificates and infrastructure across IP ranges.
tools.opsec: Censys queries are logged; route lookups through a VPN.

tools.name: BGP.tools
tools.desc: ASN and BGP prefix lookup providing routing history and peering data for network infrastructure attribution.

tools.name: SecurityTrails
tools.cost: Free tier; paid tiers for API access.
tools.desc: Passive DNS history database linking domains to historical IP addresses and vice versa; used to pivot from a single IP to related domains hosted on the same infrastructure.
tools.reliability: Historical DNS records reflect the date range indexed; recent changes may not be captured immediately.

tools.name: FreeSound
tools.cost: Free; account required for file download, not for search or preview.
tools.desc: Community audio database with Creative Commons-licensed reference recordings searchable by environment type, geography, and acoustic tag. Used for acoustic environment comparison in audio forensics workflows.
tools.opsec: Use a dedicated research account; do not use a personal account for investigation-related searches. Never upload evidentiary recordings to FreeSound; uploads are public by default. Search queries are logged server-side.
tools.reliability: Obtain at least two reference recordings from independent sources before treating an environment match as corroborating. A single-source match is insufficient for evidential purposes.

tools.name: NOAA Weather Radio Archive
tools.cost: Free, open access, no account required.
tools.desc: US government public archive of weather broadcast recordings with verified timestamps and transmitter location data. Used as a reference source for ENF comparison and acoustic environment practice exercises.
tools.opsec: Public government database; no registration required. Standard research compartmentalisation applies to any browser-based access.
tools.reliability: Verified timestamps and transmitter metadata make this a reliable ENF reference source for the Eastern Interconnection and other US grid regions. Coverage limited to US transmitters.

tools.name: ENF Toolkit
tools.desc: Bellingcat's open-source Python toolkit for automated ENF extraction and database comparison. Runs locally via command line. Used where manual Audacity ENF extraction lacks sufficient resolution.
tools.opsec: Runs entirely on the analyst's device; no data leaves the research environment. Verify package integrity against the Bellingcat GitHub repository before installation.
tools.reliability: Requires intermediate technical proficiency to install and operate. ENF database coverage varies by country and grid region; a mismatch does not confirm fabrication where database gaps exist. Document the database version and tolerance parameters used in every analysis.

tools.name: MSU Gunshot Audio Database
tools.cost: Free, open access, no account required.
tools.desc: Peer-reviewed anechoic recordings of multiple firearms for reference comparison in acoustic weapons identification workflows. Maintained by Montana State University.
tools.reliability: Covers a limited set of firearms (.308 rifle, Glock 19, Ruger SP101); not a comprehensive armoury reference. Compare findings against published methodology papers where the target weapon class is not represented.

tools.name: Google Scholar
tools.desc: Academic search engine indexing peer-reviewed papers, theses, and technical reports. Used in forensic audio workflows to locate published methodology on gunshot acoustics, blast-crack physics, and ENF analysis.
tools.opsec: Search queries are logged by Google. Use a research browser profile without personal account login for sensitive methodology searches.

tools.name: VLC Media Player
tools.desc: Open-source media player providing frame-accurate video playback for synchronising audio events to visual evidence in forensic audio and video workflows.
tools.opsec: Runs entirely on the analyst's device; no data transmitted during playback.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.desc: Command-line audio and video processing toolkit used for lossless audio extraction from video containers before forensic waveform analysis. Runs locally with no data transmission.
tools.opsec: Runs entirely on the analyst's device. Log the exact command string, tool version, and output format in the chain of custody record for every extraction.
tools.reliability: Always extract to a lossless format (WAV/PCM) without resampling or normalisation. Record the FFmpeg version; output behaviour varies across releases.

tools.name: Claude
tools.desc: Large language model used for document analysis, translation, named entity extraction, and structured reasoning tasks in AI-assisted verification workflows.
tools.opsec: Do not upload sensitive source documents, unpublished reporting, or personally identifiable information to any cloud-based AI service. All AI output requires independent verification before publication.
tools.reliability: AI output requires independent corroboration against primary sources before use. No claim rests on model output alone.

tools.name: Whisper
tools.desc: OpenAI's open-source multilingual audio transcription model. Deployable locally without data transmission, making it suitable for transcribing sensitive source material.
tools.opsec: Deploy locally to avoid uploading sensitive audio to third-party infrastructure. Never use cloud-hosted Whisper APIs for recordings containing source-identifiable content.
tools.reliability: Transcription accuracy varies by audio quality, language, and accent. All output requires manual review before use in an investigation.

tools.name: Google NotebookLM
tools.desc: Document-grounded question-answering tool with source citations. Used for structured interrogation of document collections with answers tied to uploaded source pages.
tools.opsec: Do not upload sensitive source documents, unpublished reporting, or personally identifiable information. Content is processed on Google infrastructure.
tools.reliability: Responses are grounded in uploaded documents; verify each cited passage against the source before use. Not a substitute for independent verification.

tools.name: Diffchecker
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid tiers for offline and API use.
tools.desc: Document comparison tool for identifying additions, deletions, and changes between versions of a text. Used to track changes between document drafts in investigative workflows.
tools.opsec: Use the offline desktop version for sensitive documents; the web version processes text on Diffchecker servers.

tools.name: Azure AI Document Intelligence
tools.cost: Paid; per-page pricing via Azure portal.
tools.desc: Structured data extraction from scanned documents, forms, and tables. Used for extracting named fields from official documents and invoices at scale.
tools.opsec: Content is processed on Microsoft Azure infrastructure. Confirm data handling and retention terms before uploading sensitive investigative material.
tools.reliability: Model accuracy varies by document type and scan quality. Review all extracted fields against the source document before use.

tools.name: OpenRefine
tools.desc: Open-source data cleaning and clustering tool for large structured datasets. Used to identify variant spellings and duplicate entries across entity datasets in large-scale document investigations.
tools.opsec: Runs locally in the browser; no data transmitted. Use a dedicated research browser profile.
tools.reliability: Clustering algorithms are probabilistic; human review required before asserting entity matches.

tools.name: Orbis
tools.cost: Paid; institutional licensing via Bureau van Dijk.
tools.desc: Bureau van Dijk global company database with ownership structure modelling, financial accounts, and subsidiary mapping across multiple jurisdictions.
tools.opsec: Orbis logs queries; assume commercial platform searches are visible to administrators. Use a research account not linked to your byline.
tools.reliability: Zero-employee filings reflect the reporting entity only; subsidiaries and contractors are not counted against the parent. Verify financial data against filings.

tools.name: Kyckr
tools.desc: Real-time access to primary company registry data across 170+ jurisdictions. Used where OpenCorporates coverage is insufficient or registry data needs to be current.
tools.opsec: Kyckr logs queries; assume searches are visible to platform administrators. Use a research account.

tools.name: Sayari Graph
tools.desc: Commercial corporate network mapping platform with integrated sanctions, adverse media, and trade data for cross-jurisdictional entity investigation.
tools.opsec: Platform logs queries. Use a research account not linked to your byline or institutional identity.

tools.name: WHOIS / DomainTools
tools.cost: Free for basic WHOIS; paid tiers for historical data and API.
tools.desc: Historical and current WHOIS data with registrant history. Primary tool for identifying the registrant behind a domain and pivoting on registration data.
tools.opsec: Query through a research browser profile without login sessions where possible. GDPR has redacted most registrant data post-2018; use historical snapshots for pre-redaction records.
tools.reliability: Registrant email addresses are frequently falsified or proxy-filled; treat as B2-grade identifiers requiring corroboration.

tools.name: ViewDNS.info
tools.desc: Reverse IP, DNS history, and reverse WHOIS lookup tools. Used to pivot from a registrant email to all domains registered with that address, and from an IP to all hosted domains.
tools.opsec: Query through a research browser profile. Reverse WHOIS queries are logged server-side.
tools.reliability: Shared hosting IP addresses group unrelated domains on the same server; hosting overlap is not organisational overlap.

tools.name: DomainTools Iris
tools.desc: Commercial domain intelligence platform with pivot capability on registrant fields, hosting history, and nameserver relationships for infrastructure mapping.
tools.opsec: DomainTools Iris logs all queries; assume commercial platform searches are visible and potentially accessible to the queried entity via audit trails.

tools.name: crt.sh
tools.desc: Certificate transparency log search for SSL/TLS certificates by domain. Used to surface unlisted subdomains and sibling infrastructure sharing certificates with a target domain.
tools.opsec: Queries are logged. Use a research browser profile.
tools.reliability: Certificate logs reflect issuance, not current deployment; a certificate may have been issued for infrastructure that has since been decommissioned.

tools.name: Tor Browser
tools.desc: Hardened browser routing all traffic through the Tor anonymity network. Primary tool for accessing onion-addressed services and conducting network-isolated research.
tools.opsec: Never access Tor from your primary operating system or personal browser profile. Do not resize the browser window; the default size is part of the fingerprinting defence. Set security level to Safest for onion service access.
tools.reliability: Connection failures may reflect misconfigured local firewall rules rather than censorship. Exit-node IP addresses flagged as malicious are not the investigator.

tools.name: Tails OS
tools.desc: Amnesic live operating system that routes all traffic through Tor and leaves no trace on the host machine. Used for high-sensitivity investigative sessions requiring session isolation.
tools.opsec: Boot from a dedicated USB drive rather than running as a virtual machine. Only data in an explicitly enabled encrypted persistent volume is retained between sessions.
tools.reliability: Tails warning dialogs are often informational notices about clock synchronisation or updates, not active security failures.

tools.name: VirtualBox
tools.desc: Virtualisation layer for running isolated guest operating environments. Used to create compartmentalised research environments separate from the host system.
tools.opsec: A VM on a compromised host does not provide isolation from host-level surveillance. For high-risk sessions, use Tails on dedicated hardware instead.

tools.name: Whonix
tools.desc: Dual-VM architecture routing all guest traffic through a Tor gateway. Provides persistent virtualised isolation for investigative sessions where Tails amnesia is not required.
tools.opsec: Whonix warning dialogs are frequently informational; do not interpret them as active security failures without checking the specific message.

tools.name: OnionShare
tools.desc: Generates disposable onion addresses for anonymous file transfer and receipt. Used for secure source material exchange without a permanent server.
tools.opsec: Transfer links are ephemeral and expire when the application closes. Do not share the onion address over insecure channels.
tools.reliability: OnionShare transfer links are not permanent; confirm with source that the transfer completed before closing the session.

tools.name: SecureDrop
tools.desc: Institutional onion-service platform for anonymous source submissions. Used by 60+ news organisations for source-protected document receipt.
tools.opsec: Sources must use Tor Browser to access SecureDrop. The platform protects both source and journalist identity when used correctly with Tails.
tools.reliability: SecureDrop requires institutional deployment and maintenance. Verify the newsroom's onion address from the clearnet site before use.

tools.name: Sentinel Hub
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid tiers for higher volume and API access.
tools.desc: Browser-based access to ESA Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery with date-filtered scene browser. Used for geolocation, conflict zone mapping, and environmental monitoring.
tools.opsec: Register using a research email address. Download and hash imagery files immediately on retrieval; platform archives are occasionally updated.
tools.reliability: Note the satellite pass time in UTC and sensor spatial resolution before interpreting surface features. Confirm cloud-cover metadata before drawing conclusions from optical imagery.

tools.name: Google Earth Engine
tools.cost: Free with registration; commercial use requires paid tier.
tools.desc: Cloud-based platform for large-scale satellite imagery analysis including time-series optical change detection and environmental monitoring at scale.
tools.opsec: Register using a research email address. Content and queries are processed on Google infrastructure.
tools.reliability: Time-series analysis requires cloud-free imagery for valid comparison; confirm cloud-cover metadata before interpreting results.

tools.name: Copernicus CAMS
tools.cost: Free, open access, no account required for most data.
tools.desc: EU Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service providing near-real-time atmospheric composition data including NO2, SO2, and aerosol optical depth. Used for documenting industrial air pollution and vessel emissions independently.
tools.reliability: Atmospheric NO2 plumes from industrial facilities adjacent to shipping lanes may mask or mimic vessel emissions. Single-image anomalies require temporal corroboration across multiple passes.

tools.name: NASA Earthdata
tools.desc: Access portal for MODIS, VIIRS, and Landsat datasets for environmental monitoring including fire detection, smoke plume tracking, and land-cover change analysis.
tools.opsec: Register using a research email address.
tools.reliability: MODIS fire detection has daily global coverage but 250-500m spatial resolution; verify against higher-resolution imagery for precise localisation.

tools.name: Google Earth Pro
tools.cost: Free, no account required for desktop version.
tools.desc: 3D terrain and historical imagery viewer with measurement tools. Primary tool for geolocation feature matching, shadow analysis, and conflict zone satellite overlay.
tools.opsec: Use the desktop version rather than the web version to limit data transmitted during analysis. Do not query the exact target location from a primary account or institutional IP.
tools.reliability: Historical satellite imagery may not reflect current ground conditions; confirm the imagery date before comparison. Coverage and recency vary significantly by location.

tools.name: SunCalc
tools.desc: Sun position and shadow direction calculator by location and time. Used in geolocation workflows to constrain location or timestamp from shadow direction in photographs.
tools.reliability: Mirror-image composites or flipped photographs invert shadow directions; check for digital manipulation before shadow analysis. Shadow analysis constrains but does not confirm a specific location.

tools.name: Mapillary
tools.desc: Crowd-sourced street-level imagery useful in areas without Google Street View coverage. Used for ground-level perspective comparison in geolocation workflows.
tools.reliability: Coverage is uneven; availability depends on community contribution and varies significantly by region. Always check the capture date before comparison.

tools.name: What3Words
tools.desc: 3-metre grid location identifier for precise coordinate recording and communication. Used to record and share geolocated findings with unambiguous precision.

tools.name: GeoGuessr
tools.desc: Location familiarity training tool using Street View imagery. Used to develop regional visual cue recognition skills for geolocation workflows.
tools.reliability: A training tool, not an analytical instrument. Findings require independent corroboration using primary satellite and street-level sources.

tools.name: ACLED
tools.desc: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project; geolocated conflict event database with actor, date, event type, and fatality fields. Primary structured data source for conflict zone mapping.
tools.opsec: Register using a research email address.
tools.reliability: Event locations are sourced from reporting, not field verification; coordinate precision reflects media reporting accuracy. Single-source incident reports should be treated as D3-grade pending corroboration.

tools.name: LiveUAMap
tools.desc: Real-time conflict mapping platform aggregating open-source incident reports with map display. Used as a cross-reference source for conflict event data alongside ACLED.
tools.reliability: Aggregates unverified reports; each incident requires individual source assessment before use. Do not treat LiveUAMap entries as verified without independent corroboration.

tools.name: DeepStateMap
tools.desc: Ukraine-specific territorial control mapping updated by a volunteer analyst team. Used alongside ISW assessments for independent territorial control analysis.
tools.reliability: Territorial control lines reflect analytical assessment, not confirmed physical presence on the ground. Cross-reference against geolocated primary evidence before publication.

tools.name: Kontur Population
tools.desc: Gridded population density data for assessing civilian exposure in areas of military activity. Used in conflict zone mapping to contextualise incident data.
tools.reliability: Population data reflects modelled estimates, not census-verified counts. Use as a contextual indicator rather than a precise figure.

tools.name: LinkedIn
tools.cost: Free; paid tiers for expanded search and InMail.
tools.desc: Professional network used for identifying individuals by role and employment history. Primary tool for locating potential sources with relevant professional proximity to an investigation target.
tools.opsec: Create a dedicated research account; do not use your primary professional profile. LinkedIn notifies account owners of profile views in some contexts.
tools.reliability: LinkedIn endorsements and self-reported roles are unverified; cross-check against company filings and contemporaneous press coverage before attribution.

tools.name: Signal
tools.cost: Free, open-source, no account required beyond a phone number.
tools.desc: End-to-end encrypted messaging and voice calls for secure source communications. Default channel for investigative contact in hostile or sensitive jurisdictions.
tools.opsec: Use Signal on a dedicated device registered with a non-attributable phone number. Enable disappearing messages at an appropriate interval for each contact. Signal's security depends on the endpoint; a compromised device negates the encrypted channel.
tools.reliability: Encrypted messaging protects content in transit but not metadata showing who contacted whom and when.

tools.name: Have I Been Pwned
tools.cost: Free for individual lookups; paid API access.
tools.desc: Checks whether an email address has appeared in known data breaches. Used to verify that investigative account emails have not been exposed, and as a source contact risk assessment tool.
tools.opsec: The email address queried is transmitted to the HIBP service. Use a research browser profile.
tools.reliability: Only covers breaches that have been publicly disclosed and indexed; absence of a result does not confirm an address is unexposed.

tools.name: Hunter.io
tools.desc: Email pattern discovery for organisations by domain. Returns likely email formats and known addresses for an organisation, used to identify contact routes for potential sources.
tools.opsec: Hunter.io queries are logged. Use a research account. Confirm any matched address is live before use; pattern matches are probabilistic.
tools.reliability: Email pattern matches are probabilistic and frequently outdated. Confirm the address is live before attempting contact.

tools.name: Maltego
tools.cost: Community edition free with limitations; paid from $999/yr.
tools.desc: Relationship mapping and open-source entity analysis platform. Used for visualising connections between individuals, organisations, domains, and communications infrastructure.
tools.opsec: Maltego queries run through Paterva servers and third-party transform providers; assume queries are logged. Use a research account.

tools.name: Google Images
tools.desc: Broadest open-web index for exact and visually similar image matches. Primary reverse image search tool for locating prior publication and identifying image reuse.
tools.opsec: Strip metadata from any image before uploading. Use a research browser profile without active login sessions.
tools.reliability: Index coverage varies by region and language; supplement with Yandex Images for non-Western sources. A match confirms prior publication, not the image's original context.

tools.name: TinEye
tools.cost: Free for web use; paid API access.
tools.desc: Reverse image search with chronological result ordering. Used to identify the earliest indexed appearance of an image to establish origin and detect reuse.
tools.opsec: Strip metadata before upload. Use a research browser profile.
tools.reliability: Chronological sort identifies earliest indexed appearance, not necessarily the original source. A photograph can be re-uploaded after cropping to defeat hash matching.

tools.name: Yandex Images
tools.desc: Russian-language web index consistently surfacing results missed by Western search engines. Essential supplementary reverse image search source for Russian, Eastern European, and Central Asian material.
tools.opsec: Strip metadata before upload. Use a research browser profile. Queries are processed on Yandex infrastructure.
tools.reliability: Results may include edited or contextually different versions of an image; verify each match independently.

tools.name: PimEyes
tools.desc: Facial recognition reverse image search across indexed photographs. Used where identity is the goal and public-interest grounds are established.
tools.opsec: Do not upload images of sources, witnesses, or protected individuals. Images are processed on PimEyes infrastructure. Use only where public-interest grounds are clearly established.
tools.reliability: Facial geometry matches are probabilistic; require corroborating documentary evidence before asserting identity. Treat results as B-grade pending independent corroboration.

tools.name: FotoForensics
tools.desc: Error-level analysis tool for detecting image manipulation and compositing. Used to check for signs of editing before advancing an authenticity claim.
tools.opsec: Uploads are publicly visible by default. Never upload images containing source-identifiable information, personal data, or sensitive investigative material.
tools.reliability: Compression artefacts can produce ELA signatures resembling editing; compare against an unedited reference image at the same bitrate before concluding manipulation.

tools.name: ExifTool
tools.desc: Command-line metadata extraction from image files. Used to extract GPS coordinates, camera model, timestamp, and software fields before any upload, and to strip metadata before reverse image search.
tools.opsec: Runs entirely on the analyst's device. Hash the original file with SHA-256 before any metadata extraction or stripping.
tools.reliability: EXIF timestamps can be set manually; treat camera metadata as B3-grade absent corroboration from file system or platform records.

tools.name: PACER
tools.cost: Per-page fee of $0.10; quarterly cap of $30 for small users.
tools.desc: US federal court filing system providing docket sheets, case documents, and party records across all federal district and circuit courts.
tools.opsec: Use a dedicated PACER account registered to your research identity, not a byline-linked account. PACER logs user access at the document level; assume queries are visible to opposing parties.
tools.reliability: State court records are not indexed; PACER covers federal dockets only. Check CourtListener for freely available copies before incurring fees.

tools.name: CourtListener
tools.cost: Free; RECAP archive of previously purchased PACER documents.
tools.desc: RECAP-powered archive of PACER documents with full-text search across federal filings. Used to locate freely available copies of federal court documents before incurring PACER fees.
tools.reliability: Coverage depends on prior PACER purchases by RECAP users; not all federal documents are archived. Verify document completeness against the originating PACER docket.

tools.name: Justia
tools.desc: US case law and docket search covering federal courts and selected state appellate decisions. Used for locating case law and docket information without PACER fees.
tools.reliability: Justia versions of decisions may be truncated or outdated; always verify against the originating court portal before citing.

tools.name: Find Case Law (National Archives)
tools.desc: Judgments from England and Wales courts from 2003 onwards, operated by The National Archives. Used for locating UK case law by party name or neutral citation.

tools.name: ECLI Search
tools.desc: European Case Law Identifier search covering EU member state courts. Used for locating EU jurisdiction case law by ECLI identifier or party name.
tools.reliability: Coverage varies significantly by member state; not all national courts participate fully.

tools.name: UniCourt
tools.desc: Commercial US court data aggregator providing faster bulk retrieval and entity linking across state and federal filings.
tools.opsec: Platform logs queries. Use a research account.

tools.name: ProtonMail
tools.desc: End-to-end encrypted email with Swiss jurisdiction and zero-knowledge architecture. Used for secure investigative email contact with sources who cannot use Signal.
tools.opsec: Create a ProtonMail account using Tor or a VPN for registration. Do not link it to any personal identifier. End-to-end encryption applies only when both parties use ProtonMail or PGP.
tools.reliability: Metadata (sender, recipient, timestamp) is not encrypted even with ProtonMail-to-ProtonMail messages. Content encryption does not protect against endpoint compromise.

tools.name: Mullvad VPN
tools.cost: $5/mo; anonymous account creation; cryptocurrency payment accepted.
tools.desc: No-log VPN with anonymous account creation and cryptocurrency payment option. Used to mask investigative IP addresses and isolate research traffic from personal internet use.
tools.opsec: Activate before every investigative session and verify the IP change before proceeding. Enable the kill switch to block all traffic if the VPN drops. VPN use alone is not anonymity; metadata and behavioural fingerprinting persist.
tools.reliability: A no-log policy is a contractual claim, not a technical guarantee. Route sensitive sessions through Tor for stronger anonymity where the threat model requires it.

tools.name: 1Password
tools.desc: Password manager with team vault sharing for secure credential management across investigative accounts. Used to generate and store unique passwords for all research accounts.
tools.opsec: Use a strong, unique master password. Do not store operational details or source information in shared team vaults.

tools.name: Malwarebytes
tools.desc: Endpoint malware and spyware detection used for baseline device health checks before beginning a new investigation.
tools.reliability: A clean scan does not rule out sophisticated state-level spyware such as Pegasus, which leaves minimal detectable traces on standard endpoint scanners. Use Amnesty International MVT for mobile spyware forensics.

tools.name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily)
tools.desc: Official EU journal covering public tenders and contract award notices above EU threshold values. Primary source for EU-level procurement investigation.
tools.reliability: Award dates in TED may lag actual contract signing by weeks; do not use the notice date as the contract execution date.

tools.name: Open Contracting Data Standard
tools.desc: Aggregator of OCDS-compliant national procurement data across multiple jurisdictions. Used for cross-jurisdictional procurement analysis where national portals lack standardised formats.
tools.reliability: Coverage depends on national government adoption of the OCDS standard; not all jurisdictions publish compliant data.

tools.name: OpenSpending
tools.desc: Government spending data from multiple national sources in standardised format. Used for cross-jurisdictional public expenditure analysis at transactional level.
tools.reliability: Data quality and completeness vary by contributing country. Verify figures against the originating national portal before publication.

tools.name: Contracts Finder (UK)
tools.desc: UK public contracts database from £10,000 upward with award and spending data. Used for UK-specific procurement investigation below EU threshold values.
tools.reliability: Contract value fields are disclosed minimums; variation orders and subsequent amendments regularly increase the final spend. Verify final spend against published amendments.

tools.name: Tussell
tools.desc: UK public sector contract intelligence with supplier and authority analysis. Used for pattern analysis of UK procurement awards and supplier relationships.

tools.name: Botometer
tools.desc: Machine-learning bot likelihood scoring for X/Twitter accounts. Used as one signal in social media account verification workflows.
tools.opsec: Queries are transmitted to Indiana University's OSoMe platform. Use a research account.
tools.reliability: Treat scores as B3-grade indicators requiring human review. Confidence scores reflect model certainty, not factual accuracy. High-frequency legitimate accounts (news bots, aggregators) may score highly without being inauthentic.

tools.name: X Advanced Search
tools.cost: Free; some features require X account.
tools.desc: Date-bounded and operator-filtered search on X (formerly Twitter). Used for retrieving post history within defined date ranges for account verification and incident documentation.
tools.opsec: Use a dedicated research account. Do not follow, like, or interact with accounts under investigation.
tools.reliability: X search does not return a complete historical archive; older posts may not surface. Archive content locally immediately on retrieval.

tools.name: Social Blade
tools.cost: Free; paid tiers for extended history.
tools.desc: Follower and subscriber history tracking across YouTube, X, and Instagram. Used to identify anomalous growth patterns as one signal in social media account verification.
tools.reliability: Follower growth anomalies are one indicator among many; legitimate accounts can show rapid growth during news events. Treat as a B3-grade signal requiring corroboration.

tools.name: Space-Track
tools.desc: US Space Force official orbital element database covering 27,000+ catalogued objects. Primary authoritative source for NORAD catalogue numbers, TLE data, and satellite operator attribution.
tools.opsec: Register using a research email address. Do not query specific event dates and coordinates in rapid succession from a single account.
tools.reliability: Treat TLE-derived position data as B2-grade; propagation introduces positional uncertainty that accumulates over time. TLE accuracy degrades beyond several days from the epoch.

tools.name: CelesTrak
tools.desc: Curated TLE data sets and satellite catalogue maintained by Dr T.S. Kelso. Stable civilian reference for orbital propagation calculations and constellation tracking.
tools.reliability: TLE accuracy degrades over time; use the most recent available epoch for propagation calculations. Cross-reference against Space-Track for authoritative NORAD data.

tools.name: N2YO
tools.desc: Live satellite tracking with pass predictions and TLE data. Accepts latitude, longitude, and date/time inputs to calculate which catalogued objects passed over a location during a specified window.
tools.reliability: Pass predictions are TLE-derived; accuracy depends on TLE epoch recency. Note the TLE epoch when recording orbital position calculations.

tools.name: Heavens-Above
tools.desc: Real-time satellite pass prediction and sky chart tool. Used for visual overpass planning and sensor timing in satellite intelligence workflows.

tools.name: UCS Satellite Database
tools.desc: Union of Concerned Scientists catalogue with operator, purpose, and orbit data for 6,000+ active satellites. Used to identify the operator and mission purpose of catalogued objects by NORAD number.
tools.reliability: Operator fields reflect registered ownership, not operational control, which may differ in leased or dual-use systems. The database may lag actual launch manifests by days to weeks.

tools.name: LeoLabs
tools.desc: Commercial space situational awareness platform with conjunction data and higher-precision tracking for low Earth orbit objects.
tools.reliability: Higher precision than TLE-based tools but still subject to measurement uncertainty. Consult LeoLabs documentation for specific accuracy specifications.

tools.name: SkyOSINT
tools.desc: Open-source satellite intelligence platform identifying passes near conflict zones, tracking orbital manoeuvres, and correlating RF signals with NORAD catalogue objects.

tools.name: Audacity
tools.desc: Free, open-source waveform editor and spectrogram analyser. Primary tool for ENF extraction, acoustic environment profiling, and event-sound segmentation in audio forensics workflows.
tools.opsec: Runs entirely on the analyst's device; no data leaves the research environment during spectrogram or ENF analysis. Use a dedicated research browser profile for any online documentation lookups.
tools.reliability: Spectrogram resolution is limited by FFT size; set FFT to 4096 or higher for ENF band visibility. Insufficient for high-resolution spectral work where Adobe Audition's display is required.

tools.name: Adobe Audition
tools.cost: Standalone from $22.99/mo (annual, billed monthly). Included in Creative Cloud Pro from $34.99/mo.
tools.desc: Commercial waveform editor with higher-resolution spectral frequency display than Audacity. Used for high-resolution spectrogram work where Audacity resolution is insufficient for the target signal.
tools.opsec: Disable cloud sync before opening any sensitive file. Cloud sync is enabled by default and will upload file content to Adobe servers if not explicitly turned off before opening the recording.
tools.reliability: Trial tier is adequate for spectrogram analysis; full subscription not required for basic forensic audio work. Cloud sync behaviour must be verified after every application update as settings can reset.

tools.name: MediaInfo
tools.desc: Technical metadata viewer for video and audio container formats, codec details, and bitrate. Used to assess encoding consistency in forensic media workflows.
tools.reliability: Results vary across tool versions; record the MediaInfo version alongside every analysis.

tools.name: Flightradar24
tools.cost: Free basic tier; paid subscription required for history beyond 7 days and full playback.
tools.desc: ADS-B and multilateration flight tracking platform with near-real-time position, historical playback, and aircraft registration lookup. Some operators have paid for data suppression; cross-reference against ADS-B Exchange for sensitive investigations.
tools.opsec: Use a VPN when querying aircraft linked to intelligence services or sanctioned states. Do not set up tracking alerts from an identifiable account for high-profile targets. Note that some operators request removal from Flightradar24; ADS-B Exchange does not honour those requests.
tools.reliability: Some operators have paid for data suppression; absence of a record does not confirm a flight did not occur. Cross-check registration data across at least two trackers before publishing.

tools.name: OpenSky Network
tools.cost: Free; API access available for historical queries.
tools.desc: Academic-grade open ADS-B dataset with API access for historical flight records by ICAO24 transponder code. Used to retrieve historical routes without paid-tier constraints.
tools.reliability: Coverage depends on volunteer receiver density; gaps in rural or oceanic areas are common. Note whether data is drawn from ADS-B or multilateration, as source type affects reliability.

tools.name: EDGAR (SEC)
tools.desc: US Securities and Exchange Commission filing database containing beneficial ownership disclosures, annual reports, and material event filings for publicly registered entities.
tools.opsec: Route all registry queries through a dedicated research browser profile, not your primary account.
tools.reliability: Covers SEC-registered entities only; private or non-US companies are not filed here. Beneficial ownership thresholds apply; sub-threshold holdings are not always disclosed.

tools.name: BAILII
tools.desc: British and Irish Legal Information Institute database covering case law and tribunal decisions from UK and Irish courts. Primary free-access source for UK and Irish primary law.
tools.opsec: Note the case number and jurisdiction in your research log alongside every document retrieved.
tools.reliability: Coverage begins from varying start dates depending on the court; pre-internet decisions may not be indexed. Verify decisions against originating court records before citing.

tools.name: EUR-Lex
tools.desc: Official EU legislation, case law, and regulatory notices in all member state languages. The definitive record for EU regulatory and enforcement documents; legally authentic in electronic form from 2013.
tools.opsec: Note the case number and jurisdiction in your research log alongside every document retrieved.
tools.reliability: Primary legal authority for EU law; the Official Journal published here is the legally authentic version.

tools.name: Global Legal Monitor
tools.desc: Law Library of Congress tracker for recent legislative and judicial developments in foreign jurisdictions. Used for tracking foreign legal developments by country and keyword.

tools.name: Iraq Body Count
tools.desc: Passive media surveillance conflict fatality database cross-verified from media, NGO, hospital, and official records. Largest open conflict fatality database and the reference point for passive surveillance methodology.
tools.reliability: Passive surveillance captures under 20% of total deaths in restricted-access conflict zones; use in conjunction with statistical estimation methodologies rather than as a standalone count.

tools.name: Humanitarian Data Exchange
tools.desc: UN OCHA open data platform providing mortality, displacement, and crisis datasets across active humanitarian emergencies. Used for UN-sourced independent mortality and displacement data.
tools.reliability: Data quality and completeness vary by contributing organisation and emergency. Record the dataset version and retrieval date for each download.

tools.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
tools.desc: Official WHO database of health statistics by country including baseline mortality rates, cause-of-death data, and health facility records. Used for baseline mortality calculations in excess death analysis and for health facility registry checks.
tools.reliability: Data reflects official health ministry reporting; figures may lag events by months. Conflict zones with collapsed health infrastructure routinely underreport.

tools.name: Our World in Data
tools.desc: Peer-reviewed demographic and mortality data visualisation with downloadable CSV source data. Used for baseline mortality statistics in excess death calculations.
tools.reliability: Data is sourced from peer-reviewed publications and official datasets; verify the underlying source dataset before citing for evidential purposes.

tools.name: Healthsites.io
tools.cost: Free; data downloadable, no registration required.
tools.desc: OpenStreetMap-derived global health facility map with crowdsourced facility locations and type attributes. Used to locate active medical facilities in denied-access conflict zones where official registries are unavailable.
tools.reliability: Coverage depends on community contribution and varies significantly by region. Cross-reference against WHO GHO and official ministry records to confirm active status; crowdsourced entries may be outdated.

tools.name: Planet Labs
tools.cost: Paid; registration required. Education and NGO pricing available.
tools.desc: High-cadence commercial satellite imagery with before-and-after comparison capability. Used for documenting facility destruction and confirming vessel or equipment positions during AIS gap periods.
tools.opsec: Never request satellite tasking over a subject from a byline-linked account. Treat satellite imagery coordinates as sensitive investigative material.
tools.reliability: Cloud cover and acquisition timing may prevent same-day coverage of an event. A single-pass image does not rule out activity occurring outside the satellite window.

tools.name: Maxar Open Data
tools.cost: Free for eligible events; registration required.
tools.desc: High-resolution post-event satellite imagery releases by Maxar Technologies for qualifying disasters and humanitarian events. Used for conflict damage documentation and facility verification.
tools.opsec: Record the acquisition date and sensor ID for each image retrieved; imagery is periodically updated for the same event.
tools.reliability: Releases are event-driven; not all events qualify for open data release. Verify whether a specific incident falls within the declared coverage area before relying on imagery absence.

tools.name: Meta Influence Operations Threat Reports
tools.desc: Quarterly takedown reports with indicators of compromise and attributed network descriptions published by Meta following coordinated inauthentic behaviour enforcement actions.
tools.opsec: Archive platform takedown reports as PDFs to lock the source state before content is revised or removed.
tools.reliability: Reports reflect post-enforcement analysis; they document what Meta found, not an exhaustive account of the operation. Cross-reference against independent network analysis.

tools.name: Graphika
tools.cost: Paid; free public reports on major CIB operations.
tools.desc: Network analysis platform for mapping influence operations and community clusters. Public reports on major coordinated inauthentic behaviour investigations are freely available.
tools.reliability: Public reports reflect completed investigations; the platform's commercial analysis capability exceeds what is documented in free publications.

tools.name: OSoMeNet
tools.desc: Indiana University Observatory on Social Media tools for tracking information spread, network amplification, and claim diffusion graphs across X and other platforms.
tools.opsec: Queries are transmitted to Indiana University's OSoMe platform. Use a research account.
tools.reliability: Treat outputs as B3-grade indicators requiring human review. API access to historical data is limited; recent activity is more reliably captured.

tools.name: OpenMeasures
tools.cost: Free tier; paid tiers for extended access.
tools.desc: Cross-platform fringe content search covering major alt-tech platforms. Used to track hashtag seeding and content spread across platforms before mainstream amplification.
tools.opsec: Conduct all reconnaissance from a dedicated research browser profile. Route traffic through a VPN.

tools.name: Junkipedia
tools.cost: Free for academic and journalist access.
tools.desc: Platform for monitoring accounts and content across mainstream and fringe social media. Designed for researchers and journalists tracking disinformation and influence operations.
tools.opsec: Conduct all reconnaissance from a dedicated research browser profile.

tools.name: Meedan Check
tools.desc: Collaborative claim verification and content preservation workspace. Used for structured fact-checking workflows with team annotation and archiving.

tools.name: Twilio Lookup
tools.desc: API returning carrier name, line type, porting status, and SIM swap risk signals for E.164-formatted phone numbers globally.
tools.opsec: Assume paid lookup services log queries against your identity. Route all queries through a dedicated research browser and VPN.
tools.reliability: Carrier of record reflects the current serving operator; ported numbers retain the original number prefix. Line type classification (VoIP, mobile, landline) is the most reliable field.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.desc: Open-source command-line tool for carrier attribution, VoIP detection, and Google dorking from a single E.164-formatted phone number. Aggregates multiple lookup sources in one pass.
tools.opsec: Route all queries through a dedicated research browser and VPN. Runs locally; no data transmitted beyond the configured API calls.
tools.reliability: Output quality depends on the APIs configured; crowdsourced fields are B3-grade absent corroboration.

tools.name: NumVerify
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid for higher volume.
tools.desc: API validating phone number format, carrier, country code, and line type. Used as a free-tier first check before invoking paid carrier lookup APIs.
tools.opsec: Route all queries through a dedicated research browser and VPN.
tools.reliability: Free tier is rate-limited. Ported numbers may show the original carrier; confirm with a paid lookup for definitive porting status.

tools.name: Truecaller
tools.desc: Crowdsourced global caller-ID database used to retrieve display names and spam tags associated with phone numbers. Useful for identifying how a number is labelled in the wild.
tools.opsec: Use managed attribution accounts; Truecaller logs queries. Do not use personal accounts for investigative lookups. Spam tags frequently include journalists and activists.
tools.reliability: Crowdsourced labels may be outdated or maliciously set. Treat any display name as a B3-grade identifier requiring corroboration against documentary sources.

tools.name: Epieos
tools.desc: Links phone numbers and email addresses to linked Google accounts and WhatsApp profile data. Used to surface display names, avatars, and associated accounts without direct contact.
tools.opsec: Route all queries through a dedicated research browser and VPN. Use a research account with no personal identifiers.
tools.reliability: Linked accounts reflect current profile state; data changes without notice. Treat results as B3-grade pending corroboration.

tools.name: HLR Lookup
tools.desc: Pings carrier Home Location Register for live status, roaming state, and serving network of a phone number. Provides live carrier attribution beyond static database records.
tools.opsec: Avoid HLR pings on sensitive targets; they notify carrier databases and may alert the subject or operator. Use sparingly. Route all queries through a VPN.
tools.reliability: HLR responses reflect the carrier database state at the moment of the ping. Roaming status can change within minutes.

tools.name: uBlock Origin
tools.desc: Content blocker installed into a dedicated research browser profile to reduce tracking and third-party requests during investigative browsing.
tools.opsec: Install only into the research Firefox profile, not a profile previously used for personal activity.

tools.name: Firefox Multi-Account Containers
tools.desc: Mozilla-maintained extension that isolates cookies and session storage per container, separating investigations and research personas at the browser level.
tools.opsec: Assign one container per investigation and one per persona. An uncategorised tab runs without cookie isolation. A personal login inside a research container links the two identities at the browser level.
tools.reliability: Container discipline breaks through habit, not technical failure. Confirm the active container in the tab bar before any query.

tools.name: Cover Your Tracks
tools.desc: EFF browser fingerprint testing tool used to confirm a research profile does not share a fingerprint with a personal browser before investigative use.
tools.opsec: Run from both profiles on the same day and compare the full fingerprint hash, not just the rating. Matching hashes mean the profiles are correlatable.
tools.reliability: A fingerprint that reports as protected may still be shared across a large population of similar Firefox installs. Adjust screen resolution or font list to create divergence.

tools.name: Tutanota
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid tiers for added storage and features.
tools.desc: Encrypted email provider used to register research persona addresses without requiring a phone number.
tools.opsec: Do not link the persona address to any personal account recovery option. A persona email accessible from a personal device without the VPN negates the identity separation it was built for.

tools.name: Optery
tools.cost: Free directory tier; paid tiers for managed removal.
tools.desc: Maintained directory of US data broker opt-out pages. Used as a reference index for manual removal, organised by aggregator.
tools.reliability: Use as a directory, not an automated removal service; manual submission is more reliable and produces an auditable record. Removed broker listings reappear on data refresh cycles, typically every three to twelve months.

tools.name: Google Takeout
tools.desc: Exports the data Google holds across Search, location history, YouTube, Maps and account activity. Used in a self-OSINT audit to map exposure held by the dominant search provider.

tools.name: PeakVisor
tools.cost: Free tier sufficient for terrain matching; paid tiers for added features.
tools.desc: Topographic viewer for matching ridge profiles and skyline silhouettes against named peaks during terrain triangulation.

tools.name: Geograph
tools.desc: Geographically indexed photographs of the British Isles. Used to cross-reference vernacular architecture and landscape features where Street View coverage is sparse.
tools.reliability: Coverage is strongest in the UK and Ireland; treat as a supplement to Street View and Mapillary rather than a standalone source.

tools.name: Bing Maps Streetside
tools.cost: Free; no account required to view.
tools.desc: Ground-level imagery used to confirm candidate geolocation coordinates. Coverage differs from Google Street View, particularly outside Western Europe and North America.
tools.reliability: Always check both Streetside and Street View before concluding a ground-level match is absent; their coverage and capture dates differ.

tools.name: Google Maps Street View
tools.cost: Free; no account required to view.
tools.desc: Ground-level imagery used to confirm a candidate coordinate by matching numbered frame-inventory features against the street-level view.
tools.reliability: Imagery may be dated; a match that fails today may have been correct at capture time. Note the Street View capture date; where it post-dates the image, switch to Google Earth Pro historical imagery.

tools.name: Meteostat
tools.desc: Open-access weather archive aggregating METAR and synoptic data. Used in chronolocation to cross-reference observable conditions in footage against records for a confirmed location.
tools.reliability: Weather stations may sit far from the filming location. Use to eliminate candidate dates inconsistent with observed conditions, not to confirm a specific date. Treat as weak corroboration where the station is more than 50km away over varied terrain.

tools.name: OGIMET
tools.desc: Open-access weather archive providing METAR and synoptic records with European coverage and longer date ranges. Used as a chronolocation cross-reference source.
tools.reliability: Station distance from the filming location limits precision; use to rule out inconsistent candidate dates rather than confirm one.

tools.name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS
tools.desc: Comprehensive free METAR archive for global stations, searchable by ICAO code over a date range. Used to retrieve raw weather records for chronolocation cross-reference.
tools.reliability: Record the station ICAO code and the distance to the filming location. Conditions at a distant station may differ from those at the location itself.

tools.name: Planespotters
tools.desc: Crowdsourced aircraft database cross-referencing hex addresses, tail numbers, operators and photographs. Used to confirm aircraft type and find historical operator information.
tools.reliability: Crowdsourced; useful for visual identification and historical operator data not held in official registries. Confirm identity against the ICAO hex address in primary records before attribution.

tools.name: Gephi
tools.desc: Network visualisation and analysis application. Imports graph data and applies layout algorithms, centrality measures and community detection to reveal structure. Runs locally.
tools.opsec: Runs locally; no data leaves the research environment. Keep graph files in an encrypted container with other case materials.
tools.reliability: Betweenness centrality identifies structural brokers, not the most visible actors. Remove generic shared infrastructure nodes before interpreting clusters, or they distort centrality scores.

tools.name: Wigle.net
tools.cost: Free web queries; free account required for API access.
tools.desc: Crowdsourced wardrive database resolving a wireless BSSID or SSID to geographic coordinates. Used to place a device in a neighbourhood, street or address range from network identifiers.
tools.opsec: Authenticated API queries are logged by account; anonymous web queries are logged by IP. Use an account not linked to your real identity and route through a VPN. Query terms, including BSSID strings, may be visible to the operator.
tools.reliability: Query by full BSSID, not SSID alone; common SSIDs return thousands of unrelated points. A cluster of five or more observations within roughly 50m across multiple dates supports a street-level claim; a single or dispersed observation supports only a neighbourhood claim or indicates a relocated access point.

tools.name: Maxmind GeoLite2
tools.desc: Downloadable geolocation database providing city-level and ASN-level IP mappings for offline or batch processing.
tools.opsec: Download and run locally where query privacy matters, so IP lookups do not transit a third-party service.
tools.reliability: Trustworthy at ASN and country level; treat city-level resolution as approximate and any street-level claim from IP alone as unsupported. Record the database release date, as editions update continuously.

tools.name: RIPE NCC RIS
tools.desc: Authoritative source for ASN ownership and BGP routing data. Used to verify that an ASN attribution from geo-IP matches the registered network operator.
tools.reliability: Authoritative for ASN registration and routing. Use to confirm ASN ownership before including an attribution in a report.

tools.name: Sensity
tools.cost: Free submission portal; account required for API access.
tools.desc: Deepfake detection platform specialising in face-swap and identity manipulation in video. Returns a detection confidence score and highlights flagged facial regions.
tools.opsec: Uploading a clip reveals you are investigating it. Work from a local copy and restrict uploads to a dedicated research account where the investigation is sensitive. Submitted media may be retained for model training unless opted out.
tools.reliability: No single classifier is definitive. Corroborate against a second independent tool, a perceptual finding and a provenance check. Run audio and video classifiers separately, since a voice swap on authentic video produces a diagnostic score mismatch.
